newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM says to suspend local broker from trade.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM says to suspend local broker from trade.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said on Wednesday it will ban Yamabun Co Ltd, a Tokyo-based commodity broker, from trading from August 4 to 8 for violating the Commodity Exchange Law.
TOCOM said Yamabun failed to segregate customers' money from the company's own account, in violation of Japan's Commodity Exchange Law.
The Japanese commodity broker also failed to submit correct information on the company's assets to the exchange, it said.
Yamabun is authorised to trade precious metals, rubber, cotton yarn and wool on TOCOM.
TOCOM said it and the Tokyo Grain Exchange started a joint investigation into Yamabun last October and concluded by the end of May that the broker had violated the Commodity Exchange Law.
TOCOM said it informed relevant government ministries of Yamabun's violation in June.
